description:
We are a team passionate about AI, machine learning, software development, and space technology. We enjoy exploring new ideas and turning them into practical solutions. Currently, we are building IGNIS AI, an AI-powered platform for NASA's Flame in Freefall challenge, focused on understanding fire behaviour in microgravity 
We value creativity, teamwork, curiosity, and a willingness to learn
summary:
IGNIS AI — Intelligent Gravity-Adaptive Fire Analysis System is an interactive space-combustion platform built around one interesting question: What happens to fire when gravity changes?
The homepage brings together NASA space research, real experiment images and videos, interesting facts about flames, and an animated flame visualization. The Flame Lab takes this experience further, allowing users to explore how fire behaves under different conditions, including Earth, microgravity, lunar and Martian gravity. It also covers cool flames, droplet combustion, solid-material burning, and fire extinguishment.
Users can interact with the 3D environment by rotating, zooming, selecting different flame regions, and changing environmental settings. They can also explore different scenarios, adjust the timeline, and compare flame behaviour. Each visualization comes with simple explanations to make scientific concepts easier to understand.
The platform also provides access to NASA research records and media, with links to their original sources. This helps users distinguish actual NASA research from our own visual representations.
An important note: The 3D flame visualization is an illustrative model designed for learning and exploration. It is not a scientific simulation, an exact recreation of NASA experiments, or a source of actual temperature measurements. Any hypothetical values or generated outputs are clearly presented as illustrative rather than real experimental data.
details:
The main goal of IGNIS AI is to make space-combustion research easier and more interesting to understand. Fire behaves differently when gravity changes, affecting its shape, movement, and burning process. Instead of learning everything through text, users can explore these differences through interactive 3D visualizations and access real NASA research for further learning.

The platform aims to make science more engaging and encourage people to explore how gravity, oxygen, pressure, airflow, and fuel influence fire. It also makes clear which information comes from NASA experiments and which comes from our own illustrative models.

We built the application using Next.js 15, React, TypeScript, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Drei, GLSL shaders, CSS, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, Lucide icons, and Recharts. We also use Next.js server routes to retrieve NASA media and research records. An optional Python FastAPI backend provides additional research, risk-analysis, and PDF-report features.

What makes IGNIS AI different is the way it combines NASA research, an interactive space-laboratory interface, and an animated 3D flame experience. Rather than simply displaying information, it allows users to explore and experiment with different scenarios.

While developing the platform, we focused on making it user-friendly, responsive, accessible, and easy to navigate. We also considered scientific accuracy, proper source credits, performance, and transparency. Our 3D visualization is illustrative, not a scientifically validated fire simulation, and we clearly separate actual NASA findings from hypothetical model outputs.
